items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the dual criterion of its upstairs companion: for a flat morphism of ringed topoi and a bounded below K, if each H^q(K) satisfies H^q(K) -> Rf_*f^*H^q(K) then K -> Rf_*f^*K is an isomorphism (statement lines 6367-6378). The proof passes to cohomology sheaves and uses the truncation identities H^j(Rf_*f^*K) = H^j(Rf_*tau_{<= j}f^*K) = H^j(Rf_*f^*tau_{<= j}K) to reduce to a bounded K, after which hypothesis (3) places the cohomology sheaves in the subcategory D' of the downstairs lemma and boundedness plus stability under triangles places K there (proof lines 6381-6387). The non-formal content is the truncation computation that makes the reduction legitimate. The claim is H2: one reduction of the same shape as its companion, with its own truncation identity.
